fields.english: Follow the water through the site
Rain runs off a roof into a gutter, through a first-flush pipe into a tank, and the overflow is led to a mulched basin around a fruit tree.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. It does not confirm a tank is installed, a pipe is correctly sized or water is safe to use.
How a swale holds water on a slope
Cut through a slope: runoff drops into a level ditch, soaks in and spreads under a fruit tree planted on the mound below it.

Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. A swale must be set out level on the contour and sized for the slope; on steep or unstable ground get advice before digging.
Water at the roots, not on the leaves
A raised tank feeds drip lines laid under mulch along rows of cabbage and spinach.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Pipe sizes, tank height and watering times still have to be worked out for the real beds.
Look below the surface
Cut through garden soil: mulch on top, dark living topsoil with roots and earthworms, paler subsoil with stones below, and compost being added by hand.

Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Use the site evidence checklist to add soil observations and laboratory results. This illustration does not describe measured conditions at this site.
Inside a trench bed
Cut through a trench bed: branches and bones at the bottom, then dry grass, green material, manure and topsoil, with cabbages growing in mulch on top.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Depth and fill depend on what the household has to hand.
Compost in three stages
Three compost bays side by side: fresh material, a heap half broken down, and finished dark compost ready for the beds.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Any container or heap works; the point is the three stages.
Move each crop family on, every season
Four beds seen from above — leaf crops, fruiting crops, legumes and root crops — with arrows showing each group moving to the next bed.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. The report's own calendar says what is planted where; this shows only the principle.
A guild, layer by layer
A fruit tree with a climber, a berry shrub, a clumping plant, ground cover and root crops sharing one mulched bed, roots drawn below ground.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Species and spacing must be chosen for this site; this is not its planting plan.
How a windbreak lifts the wind
Wind meets a belt of tall trees, smaller trees and shrubs, rises over it and comes down well beyond the vegetable beds sheltered behind.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Which side to plant follows the wind directions recorded for the site, not this drawing.
Low winter sun in, high summer sun out
A house with a wide eave: the high summer sun is stopped by the roof overhang while the low winter sun reaches in under it.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. The real sun angles for this latitude are in the sun and wind figure.
Zones: what you visit most sits closest
A homestead seen from above: herb and vegetable beds at the door, then chickens and fruit trees, then field crops, grazing and a belt of trees at the edge.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. The zones mapped for this site are in its own site plan.
Let the chickens prepare the next bed
A movable wire chicken run on wheels stands on one bed while the bed beside it, already cleared and manured, is ready for planting.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Stock numbers, housing and by-laws still need checking locally.
Keep a bare or green ring between grass and home
A house and water tank on a green lawn, ringed by a bare cleared strip and a gravel road that separate them from dry grassland.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Break widths and burning rules come from the local fire protection association.
Something to harvest in every season
Four beds side by side: maize, beans, pumpkin and sweet potato under a high summer sun; cabbage, carrots, onions, peas and young seedlings under a low winter sun.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. The crops and months for this site are in its planting calendar.
From the garden to a table at the gate
A shaded roadside table with crates of spinach, cabbage, tomatoes and pumpkins, seedling trays, eggs and a scale.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. Prices and demand have to be checked in the local market.
Bare plot to food garden, in stages
The same sloping plot three times: bare ground with a house and tank, then young contour beds and saplings, then a full garden with fruit trees.
Concept illustration, the same in every report. It is not a picture of this site. How fast the real site changes depends on water, labour and money.
A living landscape, layer by layer
Concept illustration. Species, spacing and the layers present must be checked for this site; this is not its measured vegetation profile.
Trees mentioned in this section
Catalogue illustrations, not site photographs or identification evidence. Read the advice and confirm local suitability before choosing plants.
